definition: The rate at which a component transfers energy from the current, in watts: $P = IV$, where $I$ is the current in it and $V$ is the p.d. across it.
The energy a current transfers to a component, in joules: $E = IVt$, with the current $I$ in A, the p.d. $V$ across the component in V and the time $t$ in s.
A unit of energy (kW h): the energy transferred by an appliance of power 1 kW in 1 hour, equal to $3.6 \times 10^{6}$ J; electricity bills charge per kW h.
